requirements.requirement: Bring node1's unconfigured lan-b-facing interface (vtnet2) into service as its own OPNsense zone with an address on lan-b
requirements.summary: vtnet2 was administratively enabled, added as a new opt1/'LANB' interface in config.xml with static 10.60.60.1/24, and configctl interface reconfigure opt1 applied the config live, confirmed by ifconfig showing inet 10.60.60.1/24 and description 'LANB (opt1)' on vtnet2. A matching firewall pass rule for the new zone was also confirmed present via pfctl -s rules.
node3's ens7 was assigned 10.60.60.2/24 and directly pinged node1's 10.60.60.1 with 0% loss and TTL 64 (single hop), confirming reachability on the new lan-b segment.

requirements.requirement: node3 reaches node2 on lan-a through node1
requirements.summary: With a host route on node3 to 10.100.25.11 via node1's lan-b address and OPNsense's pre-existing automatic outbound NAT covering the new opt1/lan-b network, node3 successfully pinged node2 (10.100.25.11) with TTL 63 (one router hop), and node1's pf state table showed the ICMP flow being NAT-translated and forwarded, directly demonstrating traversal through node1.

requirements.requirement: (supplemental) node1 restart evidence: baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boottime (17:31:33) captured, shutdown -r now acknowledged, two subsequent SSH attempts timed out confirming a real outage, then boottime changed to 17:41:09, and post-restart checks show the opt1 interface, its firewall rule, and node3/node2 reachability through node1 all recovered.

requirements.requirement: (supplemental) node2 restart evidence: baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (2b3a8d87) captured, sudo shutdown -r now acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed to 59760cb9 with new uptime, ens2 address and node3->node2-through-node1 connectivity recovered. However, unlike node1, no intermediate timed-out/failed connection attempt was captured to directly confirm the outage window, so the bounded-disruption portion of the transition is inferred from timestamps rather than directly observed.

requirements.requirement: (supplemental) node3 restart evidence: baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (88feca03) captured, sudo shutdown -r now acknowledged, post-restart boot_id changed to 1e873999, and recovered state shows persisted ens7 static IP/route from /etc/network/interfaces.d and successful pings to both node1 and node2. As with node2, no direct outage/connection-timeout evidence was captured during the restart window.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the public task were satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence: node1's unconfigured lan-b-facing NIC (vtnet2) was brought up as a new OPNsense opt1/'LANB' zone with static 10.60.60.1/24 and a firewall pass rule; node3 was configured with 10.60.60.2/24 and directly pinged node1 successfully (TTL64); and node3 reached node2 on lan-a through node1 via a host route plus OPNsense's automatic outbound NAT, verified end-to-end with a successful ping (TTL63) and corroborating pf NAT state-table entries. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity changes and post-restart functional recovery confirmed for all; node1's restart additionally included direct evidence of a connection-timeout outage window, while node2 and node3 lacked that same direct outage confirmation. Diagnostic mutations used to disambiguate node1's two unconfigured NICs were bounded and fully reverted, leaving no residue.
limitations: The exact contents of the base64-encoded Python script used to edit /conf/config.xml (cmd-9c22d783e1af4731) were not directly inspected in the trace; its effect was instead verified indirectly through subsequent config reads and live interface/firewall state, which is sufficient but not a full byte-level confirmation of the edit.

node2 and node3 restarts lack a captured intermediate failed/timed-out connection attempt (unlike node1), so the bounded-disruption portion of their restart transitions is inferred from boot-identity and uptime changes rather than directly observed mid-outage.

Reachability from node3 to node2 depends on NAT and a manually-added host route on node3 rather than symmetric routing on node2; this works as demonstrated but was not tested for reverse-initiated traffic from node2 to node3, which the task did not require.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor performed several bounded, diagnostic mutations to identify which unconfigured NIC (vtnet1 vs vtnet2) on node1 faced lan-b vs lan-a: temporary IPs 172.30.30.11/24 and 172.30.30.12/24 were added to node2's and node3's ens7 interfaces (cmd-1dc90aa1e02d4aa2, cmd-2f30094df1c14ccc, cmd-ad6e188423c54236, cmd-7454e2a25ef249b2) to generate broadcast/ARP traffic captured via tcpdump on node1's vtnet1/vtnet2, correctly mapping vtnet2 to node3/lan-b. These temporary addresses were fully removed afterward (cmd-3ee7f84821da4114, cmd-469b1979d67a4f1f), and node2's unused ens7 was returned to a down state (cmd-bedf2673988c49ef) since it played no role in node2's final configuration. No residue, failed services, or unsafe exposure remained in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot; temp-file listings show only expected session/reboot artifacts. The interface-mapping approach was a reasonable, low-risk way to resolve real ambiguity between two unconfigured NICs before making the final config.xml edit, and all test state was cleanly reverted.
